transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-17 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Alice (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jenna (CTO, Lumina Med), Omar (Identity), Priya (Security), Brian (SRE)

Summary: quick SSO and provisioning walkthrough focused on SAML/SCIM and RBAC design. A few clarifying questions about private deploys for PHI and audit log retention.

[00:00] Alice: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um - quick intros 'cause I think some folks are joining from different teams. I'm Alice, AE at Redwood.
[00:10] Jenna: Hi all, Jenna here, CTO at Lumina Med. We're mainly here to lock down the SSO/SCIM flow and make sure RBAC maps to our least privilege model.
[00:18] Omar: Omar, Identity lead. We run Okta for core workforce, but we're evaluating auto-provisioning cadence for contractors and service accounts.
[00:25] Marcus: Marcus from Redwood infra, I own the SSO and RBAC patterns on our side, and can walk through SCIM attributes and sample mappings.
[00:31] Priya: Priya, security. We're SOC 2 Type II in process, need to understand audit logs and key management for PHI paths.
[00:38] Alice: Great. Quick agenda: SAML config bits (ACS / EntityID / NameID formats), SCIM provisioning and group-to-role mappings, RBAC roles and least privilege, and then logging/KMS questions.

[00:52] Marcus: I'll start with SAML. On Redwood side the SP expects an ACS URL like https://api.redwood.ai/sso/saml/acs and an entity id, we can provide SP metadata XML. We support both email and persistent NameID formats - preferred is email for most customers.
[01:08] Omar: Are you supporting both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows? We often do IdP-initiated for Okta.
[01:12] Marcus: Yes, both. Small caveat: if you use IdP-initiated you need to ensure the relay-state is consistent for route selection if you're using multi-tenant orgs.
[01:25] Jenna: Good, and cert rotation - how does Redwood surface cert changes? We rotate every 90 days on our end.
[01:31] Marcus: We support metadata push/pull. We recommend either automated metadata exchange or a scheduled manual rotation cadence. We'll send a notification 30 days prior; customer can send new cert via the admin console or the SP metadata.

[01:48] Omar: For SCIM, what attributes do you expect? group or role membership? we have a few service groups for engineers, product, and a clinical ops group.
[01:56] Marcus: SCIM v2 with group provisioning mapping to roles. Typical attributes: displayName, members (user ids), externalId, and then we map SCIM groups to Redwood roles (org-admin, app-admin, billing, dev, observer). We can show a manifest.
[02:10] Priya: We have strict rules for contractor accounts - they should only get observer access unless explicitly onboarded. Can SCIM handle provisioning cadence, like expire after 30 days?
[02:19] Marcus: SCIM itself doesn't enforce expiry, but a provisioning pipeline can set an external attribute like accountExpiry and sync. Our platform honors a "suspended" flag; we can also integrate with an IdP lifecycle script to disable.

[02:35] Brian: From SRE perspective: do you create local user objects in Redwood or are they purely federated? We want to avoid local creds for service accounts.
[02:42] Alice: Best practice is federated accounts for human users; for machine/service accounts you can use API keys scoped to roles, or leverage short-lived tokens with KMS-backed signing. We can show a model where service accounts are created as 'machine' entities with limited scope.

[02:58] Jenna: About RBAC - our matrix is pretty granular. We need least-privilege: product devs need model invoke and embed, SRE needs full invocation logs, security needs audit-read, billing needs usage-only. How does Redwood map those?
[03:10] Marcus: We generally recommend these roles: org-admin (full admin), team-admin (manage routes/models for a team), developer (invoke and create routes but not billing), billing (view usage/billing only), observer (metrics/read-only), security-audit (access to audit logs and export). You can create custom roles too.
[03:25] Priya: Is audit-log access paged with retention windows? For SOC 2 we need 365 days of immutable logs.
[03:32] Marcus: Hosted customers get 365-day retention for standard; dedicated and private can extend retention and we support append-only audit streams and S3 archival with object-lock for immutability. For high-regulated PHI you might want private with KMS/HSM control.

[03:49] Omar: Data residency: our legal is insisting on US-only processing for PHI. Do you support region pinning?
[03:55] Alice: Yes - Redwood supports region pinning. For PHI we typically recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated in a US region with customer-managed keys. We'll document the deployment modes and help you choose.

[04:10] Jenna: On encryption - is data encrypted at rest by default and can we bring our own keys?
[04:15] Marcus: At rest encryption is default. BYOK is supported in Dedicated/Private via KMS (AWS KMS or HSM). We also support envelope encryption for artifacts like model caches and KV caches - though quick note, KV cache was previously transcribed as K-V cash in some docs, haha.
[04:32] Priya: For key rotation, do you allow rotation without downtime? We need to ensure sessions don't break mid-flight.
[04:37] Marcus: We support asymmetrical rotation patterns: you can rotate keys and we can orchestrate re-encryption progressively. Session tokens are signed; rotation window is orchestrated to avoid breaking in-flight tokens. We'll share the rotation playbook.

[04:55] Alice: Let's talk about SCIM mapping patterns. Marcus do you want to share the screen? (screen share noise)
[05:02] Marcus: Sure - showing sample manifest now. Example: SCIM Group "redwood-developers" -> Redwood role "developer"; group attribute externalId maps to team id. For contractors, we recommend a "contractor" group mapped to "observer" and set externalExpiry attribute.
[05:22] Omar: Can we do nested groups? We use nested in Okta for inheritance.
[05:28] Marcus: We support nested groups if the IdP flattens them in the SCIM payload, otherwise we recommend explicit top-level groups to avoid complexity.

[05:40] Jenna: SAML attributes - what about provisioning name id? We're using email address as the primary key but sometimes we use employeeNumber for contractors.
[05:47] Marcus: You can map either; we recommend stable immutable identifier. Email is ok if you have strict email hygiene. EmployeeNumber is better if users change emails. We'll accept 'nameid-format: persistent' or 'email'.

[06:00] Priya: Audit log format - do you provide raw events? Our SOC auditor wants a CSV export of auth events and admin actions.
[06:07] Marcus: We stream raw events to a customer-owned S3 bucket (for Dedicated/Private) and provide queryable logs via the Console for Hosted. We can provide scheduled exports or a one-off export for audit review.

[06:24] Brian: For the staging cutover test, what does success look like? We want to validate SSO login, SCIM provisioning of two test users, group -> role mapping verification, and audit event for user create + admin change.
[06:33] Alice: Yep, that's the checklist we'll use. Marcus will run the SCIM sync, Brian will validate accounts in staging, Priya will confirm audit events, and Omar will provide cert/test users.

[06:46] Omar: A few edge cases: what about service accounts - we want them tagged differently and not provisioned via SCIM.
[06:52] Marcus: Service accounts should be created as machine identities. We recommend issuing scoped API keys with restricted permissions and limited TTL. We'll also show how to attach tags to identify PHI-related service accounts.

[07:05] Jenna: Are there any known gotchas for SAML with older IdPs? We have a couple of legacy apps.
[07:10] Marcus: Some older IdPs have quirks around NameID format and assertion signing algorithms (RSA-SHA1 is still seen sometimes). We require SHA256 signing; if you have a legacy IdP that can't do that, we can work with a proxy or short-term workaround, but it's a security concern.

[07:28] Priya: Regarding SOC2 evidence - does Redwood provide templates for evidence collection (like access control policies, change logs)?
[07:34] Alice: Yes, we maintain SOC2 and ISO docs and can share the compliance pack once NDA/PO is in place. There's a security questionnaire and an evidence bundle. We'll add your legal to the distribution list.

[07:48] Marcus: Just to clarify RBAC granularity: roles are first-class and can be scoped to org or team. Example: 'team-admin:prod-search' vs 'org-admin'. We also have policy-level controls for model-level allow/deny.
[08:02] Omar: Model-level allow/deny? We have some classified models for internal only.
[08:06] Marcus: Yes you can pin a route to a restricted model and use policy to limit which roles can call that route.

[08:17] Jenna: I want to call out compliance: if we keep PHI on Redwood hosted, we need BAAs and explicit support for HIPAA. Do you have that?
[08:24] Alice: Redwood provides BAAs for Dedicated and Private customers; hosted can be evaluated case-by-case. We'll route the legal ask to our enterprise team.

[08:35] Brian: For logging: how quickly are logs available post-event? We need near-real-time for incident response.
[08:40] Marcus: Logs are available in near real time (under 30s) in the Console. Archived exports to S3 are eventually consistent but near real-time streaming via Kinesis or Pub/Sub is available for Dedicated/Private.

[08:55] Omar: Any limits on SCIM calls per minute? We might do bulk provisioning during onboarding.
[09:00] Marcus: Rate limits exist for hosted tenants; we provide burst allowances. For large onboardings we recommend a staged sync or use the bulk user import API. We'll coordinate a temporary bump for your cutover.

[09:12] Priya: On SAML logout - do you support single logout (SLO)? We sometimes need immediate deprovisioning.
[09:18] Marcus: We support SLO via HTTP-Redirect/POST binding. Also, SCIM deprovisioning will suspend accounts; we recommend that for immediate access removal.

[09:30] Alice: Quick note on metadata exchange - I'll attach the SP metadata and a short how-to for Okta/OneLogin and general SCIM manifest. Also a link to RBAC example. (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/sso-scim-rbac)

[09:46] Jenna: Great - on timelines we are targeting a pilot in staging by 2025-06-25 and production cutover late July.
[09:52] Alice: That seems reasonable. We'll aim for the mid-June deliverables then the staging test.

[10:00] Marcus: A minor transcription glitch I've seen: references to KV cache sometimes get transcribed incorrectly in meeting notes. For clarity, our KV cache stores prefix caches and is encrypted at rest.

[10:12] Priya: Ok final compliance check - can you provide a sample SOC2 control mapping for SSO/SCIM? We need to map control CC6 for access provisioning to your platform features.
[10:21] Alice: Yes - we'll include a control mapping doc in the compliance pack.

[10:30] Omar: One last question - if we go Dedicated versus Hosted, how different is the SSO/SCIM setup?
[10:36] Marcus: Functionally it's the same; Dedicated gives you private network, BYOK, and longer data retention options. Hosted is easier to get started but has less BYOK capability. Configuration endpoints (ACS/EntityID/SCIM base URL) will differ by deployment and we'll provide the correct metadata.

[10:52] Brian: Let's record the success criteria again: SSO login + SCIM provisioning + RBAC mapping + audit events. If we see gaps, we'll iterate.

[11:03] Alice: Recap of next steps: I (Alice) share SP metadata + docs; Marcus shares RBAC matrix + SCIM manifest; Omar supplies IdP artifacts; Brian and Marcus schedule staging smoke test. We'll sync up in follow-up.

[11:20] Jenna: Thank you, that was helpful.
[11:23] Alice: Thanks everyone, we'll follow-up with links and action items.

End of transcript.

Notes: minor transcription quirks present (names sometimes mis-cased; acronyms like KMS/HSM sometimes transcribed as K-M-S). References shared: https://redwood.ai/docs/sso-scim-rbac (Redwood doc), SP metadata will be attached in follow-up.
